text:
mike_sales: Quick heads-up - DeltaSystems POC can't see traces in Redwood Console even though Splunk shows x-request-id. Their logs in GCP also don't show trace linkage. Need a short presales swarm.

elaine_se: @mike_sales please paste a raw log line and any trace headers (traceparent or X-Cloud-Trace-Context). Also confirm whether they're sending logs via otel-collector -> googlecloud exporter or forwarding to Splunk first.

mike_sales: They sent this log: ```json
{"ts":"2026-02-25T09:12:10Z","level":"info","msg":"completed","request_id":"ds-77","trace":"4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736"}
``` Header: `traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01`

novak_eng: Likely mapper issue. Cloud Logging needs `entry.trace = "projects/PROJECT/traces/TRACE_ID"` to link logs to traces. If the collector emits raw trace id only, the UI won't show it. Also check that fluentd/splunk forwarder doesn't cast hex trace to integer (loses leading zeros).

sylvia_sre: Check for 429s/quota as well - dropped exports will make it appear missing. Quick check: our log-forwarder metrics show retry/429 spikes?

logbot: Found 429s from delta-prod to logging.googleapis.com between 08:58-09:05 UTC; throttling limit was 45 rps.

elaine_se: For POC demo, recommend: 1) set SDK sampling=100% temporarily; 2) ensure exporter uses service account with roles/logging.logWriter and roles/cloudtrace.agent; 3) set collector batch size >=256 and enable retries/backoff; 4) map `trace` -> `entry.trace` with projects/<id>/traces/<id>; 5) keep x-request-id as a separate top-level field for Splunk correlation.

novak_eng: Example otel-collector snippet I sent them: 
```yaml
exporters:
  googlecloud:
    project: "delta-prod"
processors:
  batch:
service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [googlecloud]
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [googlecloud]
```
Also ensure fluentd has `keep_time_key true` and no casting on trace field.

sylvia_sre: Once they switch to service account & bump batch sizes, watch for a drop in 429s. If still high, increase sink throughput or shard exporters.

mike_sales: They flipped to service account, disabled cast, set sampling=100% and bumped batch. New sample: ```json
{"ts":"2026-02-25T09:14:22Z","level":"info","msg":"completed","x-request-id":"ds-77","trace":"4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736","trace_full":"projects/delta-prod/traces/4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736"}
```

novak_eng: Perfect. `trace_full` into `entry.trace` will link logs to Cloud Trace and Redwood Console. For Splunk correlation they can search x-request-id.

elaine_se: I'll add this checklist to the sales playbook: sampling=100% for POC, service account roles, batch size >=256, map trace->entry.trace, no cast, watch 429s.

mike_sales: Thanks all - demo greenlit. Closing thread on my side :tada:
